strengths: The proposed Mixture-of-Visual-Thoughts (MoVT) paradigm is highly intuitive and addresses a critical limitation of current vision-language reasoning models, which typically specialize in either textual reasoning or visual grounding but struggle to generalize across both.

The AdaGRPO algorithm is mathematically elegant and well-designed. By separating the advantage calculation into mode-relative advantage (for prefix tokens) and rollout-level advantage (for thinking process tokens), the framework successfully guides both mode selection and reasoning quality simultaneously.

The paper presents a very comprehensive evaluation across 8 diverse benchmarks, showing consistent improvements of AdaVaR over baseline models (Qwen2.5-VL) and other state-of-the-art visual reasoning models. Notably, AdaVaR-7B surpasses GPT-4o in average performance.

The ablation studies and analytical sections (such as SFT-guided adaptive reasoning baselines, learning dynamics visualization, and category-wise mode selection ratios) are exceptionally thorough and provide deep insights into how the model acquires its adaptive reasoning skills.
weaknesses: The evaluation relies on an ad-hoc 'mode-switching' heuristic at inference time to handle repetitive loops. It is unclear how often this mode-switching is triggered during evaluation and what the performance would be if the model strictly followed its first chosen mode prefix autoregressively.

The study is limited to only two reasoning modes (text-based and bounding-box grounded). While the authors discuss scaling to more modes in the future work, demonstrating the framework's scalability to a third mode (e.g., short-chain / direct answering) would have significantly strengthened the generalizability claim.

The RL training phase requires generating 2n rollouts per question with forced prefixes, which introduces non-trivial computational overhead. A more detailed discussion on the training efficiency compared to standard GRPO would be helpful.

strengths: The core idea of adaptively selecting the visual reasoning mode (pure natural language CoT vs. visually-grounded CoT) based on context is highly intuitive and addresses a real limitation where single-mode models excel in one area but fail in another.

The proposed AdaGRPO algorithm is a well-designed adaptation of GRPO. The prefix-guided mode exploration avoids mode collapse during sampling, and the mode-relative advantage calculation provides a solid mathematical way to optimize the mode selection prefix.

Extensive and thorough evaluation across 8 diverse benchmarks, demonstrating consistent and clear improvements over strong baselines like Qwen2.5-VL. Achieving results where AdaVaR-7B surpasses GPT-4o on average is impressive.

Comprehensive ablation studies and analysis (such as the upper bound of adaptive reasoning, the necessity of mode-specific prefixes, and the learning dynamics curve) provide strong credibility and deep insights into the training process.
weaknesses: The formulation is currently limited to two modes. While the authors discuss extending to more modes in the appendix, scaling to M > 2 modes might make the advantage calculation and uniform prefix exploration more complex and computationally expensive.

Training overhead is potentially high: generating 8 rollouts per sample (4 for text, 4 for ground) is computationally demanding, especially with the long completion lengths typical in reasoning models.

The performance during the RL stage is bounded by the availability of datasets with verifiable answers. For open-ended general visual reasoning tasks without exact matches or rule-based verification, implementing this framework would be much more challenging.

strengths: A highly novel and well-motivated paradigm (Mixture-of-Visual-Thoughts) that unifies textual reasoning and visually-grounded reasoning within a single VLM, allowing the model to adaptively select the best mode depending on the context.

The proposed AdaGRPO algorithm elegantly solves the mode-collapse problem in reinforcement learning by forcing prefix-guided exploration and calculating a standard-normal-based mode-relative advantage to steer mode selection.
Extensive evaluation across 8 diverse benchmarks demonstrates significant improvements over the base model (Qwen2.5-VL) and outperforms strong closed/open-source baselines including GPT-4o.
Thorough analysis and ablation studies, showing why SFT fails at mode selection, why both components of AdaGRPO are necessary, and providing detailed training dynamics and qualitative examples.
weaknesses: High computational overhead: Performing VLM reinforcement learning with multiple rollouts per prompt is expensive, requiring 32 A100 GPUs for 29 hours for the 7B model.

Scalability to more than two modes: The proposed CDF-based mode-relative advantage formulation in Section 3.3.1 is designed for binary mode comparison. It is unclear how easily this scales when more than two modes are introduced.

Role of the test-time mode-switching heuristic: The paper mentions that if the model gets stuck in a loop during inference, it switches modes. It is important to isolate the performance gain of this rule-based test-time trick from the RL-learned policy via an ablation.

strengths: Compelling and highly timely motivation: dynamically unifying and selecting between text-based reasoning and visually-grounded reasoning is a very natural and effective step forward for multimodal chain-of-thought models.

Well-designed RL framework (AdaGRPO): the prefix-guided exploration, mode-relative advantage calculation, and curriculum scheduling are technically sound and successfully address the mode-bias problem inherent in traditional RL algorithms.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: the authors evaluate their method on 8 diverse visual reasoning benchmarks (covering math, spatial, and general visual perception) and show consistent improvements over strong baselines, even matching or outperforming larger models like Qwen2.5-VL-7B (by AdaVaR-3B) and GPT-4o (by AdaVaR-7B).

Thorough ablation and qualitative analysis: the paper includes extensive supplementary experiments examining the SFT data ratio, prefix formats, attention visualization, and curriculum learning, making the technical findings highly convincing and robust.
weaknesses: The test-time 'mode-switching' mechanism (switching modes if the model gets stuck in a repetitive loop) introduces a heuristic element. It is not fully clear how much of the performance gain is due to this fallback strategy versus the learned policy itself.

The visual reasoning modes are restricted to only two options (pure text vs. bounding box grounding). Although extensions to more modes are discussed in the appendix, the empirical validation of the scaling properties of 'width extension' (e.g., adding tool use) remains limited.

The visually-grounded mode relies heavily on precise bounding box coordinate outputs. The paper would benefit from a more detailed analysis of the model's robustness to inaccurate coordinates generated during the thinking process.

strengths: Clear and impactful motivation: The paper addresses a highly relevant and practical problem, showing that while text-based multi-modal reasoning models excel at abstract reasoning (like math), visually-grounded models are better at localization and avoiding hallucination. The unification of these complementary modes is highly intuitive.

Novel and sound methodology: The proposed AdaVaR framework, along with the AdaGRPO algorithm, is well-designed. Specifically, the prefix-guided exploration (forcing rollouts from both modes) and the mode-relative advantage mechanism elegantly address the limitations of vanilla GRPO in adaptive action spaces.

Comprehensive and convincing evaluation: The authors evaluate on 8 diverse benchmarks spanning mathematical reasoning and general/spatial/perceptual visual tasks. The results show consistent improvements, with AdaVaR-7B outperforming both Qwen2.5-VL-7B and GPT-4o on average.

Extensive analysis and ablation studies: The paper provides thorough empirical insights, including learning curves of mode selection, proof of the necessity of the RL stage over multi-stage SFT, dataset-level and task-level selection analyses, and robustness testing against image noise.
weaknesses: Scalability of the exploration strategy: While the approach works exceptionally well for two modes, exploring $k$ modes using prefix-guided exploration linearly increases the computational complexity of the rollout stage (since the model must generate rollouts for each mode). Although the appendix suggests filtering to top-$j$ modes, this scalability is not empirically verified.

Dependence on verifiable rewards and high-quality SFT: Like other R1-style frameworks, AdaVaR relies on rule-based verifiers for reward calculation, which limits the training data to tasks with exact or highly structured answers. It also requires highly curated SFT data for the cold-start phase, which might limit its adaptability to more open-ended visual reasoning tasks.

strengths: The proposed Mixture-of-Visual-Thoughts (MoVT) paradigm is highly intuitive and tackles a critical trade-off in multimodal large language models: balancing abstract semantic reasoning with precise visual grounding.

The AdaGRPO algorithm is a novel and well-designed adaptation of GRPO. It effectively solves the mode-collapse issue during reinforcement learning rollouts by utilizing prefix-guided exploration and explicit mode-relative advantage estimation via cumulative distribution functions.

Extensive empirical evaluation across 8 diverse benchmarks shows significant and consistent performance improvements. Notably, AdaVaR-7B outperforms several competitive visual reasoning baselines and surpasses GPT-4o on average accuracy.

The manuscript is exceptionally thorough, offering detailed supplementary analysis including investigations on training/inference efficiency, curriculum learning, robustness to image noise, and attention visualizations.
weaknesses: During evaluation, a mode-switching fallback mechanism is triggered when a model gets stuck in repetitive logic (Section 4.1). It is unclear whether this retry heuristic was also applied to the baselines. If not, this might introduce an unfair evaluation advantage.

The empirical evaluation is limited to a binary choice between two modes (text-based and visually-grounded). While Appendix C.6.1 outlines extension paths, demonstrating the framework's scalability with a third active mode (e.g., tool-use or direct-answer) would strongly bolster the generality claims.
